concept.name: Zero-lag exponential moving average
concept.definition: A lag-corrected EMA (John Ehlers and Ric Way, 'Zero Lag (Well, Almost)', TASC 2010): an EMA applied to de-lagged data — price plus the difference between the current price and the price (n-1)/2 bars ago — compensating for the EMA's inherent lag.
concept.intuition: Pre-correct the data for the lag you know the EMA will add, so the smoothed output lands close to the current price.
concept.mechanics: Form the adjusted series Z_t = P_t + (P_t - P_{t-lag}) with lag = floor((n-1)/2), then take a standard n-period EMA of Z. The construction is related to Mulloy's DEMA/TEMA lag-cancellation idea.
concept.formula: lag = floor((n-1)/2); Z_t = P_t + (P_t - P_{t-lag}); ZLEMA_t = EMA_n(Z)_t with k = 2/(n+1).
concept.failure_modes: The de-lagging term amplifies noise and overshoots on sharp reversals; in sideways markets it whipsaws more than a plain EMA.
concept.misconceptions: Zero lag is aspirational: the correction removes the systematic EMA lag in smooth trends but cannot anticipate turning points, where lag remains.
concept.example: For n = 10, lag = 4; if P_t = 105 and P_{t-4} = 100, the EMA is applied to 110 instead of 105, pulling the average up toward the trending price.

citations.source: Zero-Lag Exponential Moving Average - Tulip Indicators
